title: Rigveda 8.83: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.83: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.83 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 649v-650r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.83.1-3 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 6, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 649v
translation.original_text:
1de̱vānā̱m id avo̍ ma̱hat tad ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe va̱yam | vṛṣṇā̍m a̱smabhya̍m ū̱taye̍ ||
2te na̍ḥ santu̱ yuja̱ḥ sadā̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | vṛ̱dhāsa̍ś ca̱ prace̍tasaḥ ||
3ati̍ no viṣpi̱tā pu̱ru nau̱bhir a̱po na pa̍rṣatha | yū̱yam ṛ̱tasya̍ rathyaḥ ||
translation.text:
1WE choose unto ourselves that high protection of the Mighty Gods That it may help and succour us.
2May they be ever our allies, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Far-seeing Gods who prosper us.
3Ye furtherers of holy Law, transport us safe o'er many woes, As over water-floods in ships.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 649v (numbered 71v by the scribe) (OPenn image 650, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.82.2 ‹-sutāsaḥ mādayiṣṇavaḥ piba dadhṛk›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 650r (numbered 72r by the scribe), begins in RV 8.83.4 ‹vāmam varuṇa śaṃsyam vāmam›. Verses 8.83.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1devānām | it | avaḥ | mahat | tat | ā | vṛṇīmahe | vayam | vṛṣṇām | asmabhyam | ūtaye
2te | naḥ | santu | yujaḥ | sadā | varuṇaḥ | mitraḥ | aryamā | vṛdhāsaḥ | ca | pra-cetasaḥ
3ati | naḥ | viṣpitā | puru | naubhiḥ | apaḥ | na | parṣatha | yūyam | ṛtasya | rathyśaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 8.83.4-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 6, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 650r
translation.original_text:
4vā̱maṁ no̍ astv aryaman vā̱maṁ va̍ruṇa̱ śaṁsya̍m | vā̱maṁ hy ā̍vṛṇī̱mahe̍ ||
5vā̱masya̱ hi pra̍cetasa̱ īśā̍nāśo riśādasaḥ | nem ā̍dityā a̱ghasya̱ yat ||
6va̱yam id va̍ḥ sudānavaḥ kṣi̱yanto̱ yānto̱ adhva̱nn ā | devā̍ vṛ̱dhāya̍ hūmahe ||
7adhi̍ na indraiṣā̱ṁ viṣṇo̍ sajā̱tyā̍nām | i̱tā maru̍to̱ aśvi̍nā ||
8pra bhrā̍tṛ̱tvaṁ su̍dāna̱vo 'dha̍ dvi̱tā sa̍mā̱nyā | mā̱tur garbhe̍ bharāmahe ||
9yū̱yaṁ hi ṣṭhā su̍dānava̱ indra̍jyeṣṭhā a̱bhidya̍vaḥ | adhā̍ cid va u̱ta bru̍ve ||
translation.text:
4Dear wealth be Aryaman to us, Varuṇa dear wealth meet for praise: Dear wealth we choose unto ourselves.
5For Sovrans of dear wealth are ye, Âdityas, not of sinner's wealth, Ye sapient Gods who slay the foe.
6We in our homes, ye Bounteous Ones, and while we journey on the road, Invoke you, Gods, to prosper us.
7Regard us, Indra, Vishṇu, here, ye Aṣvins and the Marut host, Us who are kith and kin to you.
8Ye Bounteous Ones, from time of old we here set forth our brotherhood, Our kinship in the Mother's womb.
9Then come with Indra for your chief, as early day, ye Bounteous Gods Yea, I address you now for this.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 650r (numbered 72r by the scribe) (OPenn image 650, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.83.4 ‹vāmam varuṇa śaṃsyam vāmam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 650v (numbered 72v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.84.6 ‹-viśvāḥ asmabhyam su-kṣitīḥ vāja-draviṇasaḥ›. Verses 8.83.4-9 end on this page; 8.83.4 begins on fol. 649v (numbered 71v by the scribe).

5vāmasya | hi | pra-cetasaḥ | īśānāsaḥ | riśādasaḥ | na | īm | ādityāḥ | aghasyayat
6vayam | it | vaḥ | su-dānavaḥ | kṣiyantaḥ | yāntaḥ | adhvan | ā | devāḥ | vṛdhāya | hūmahe
